questions.q: What does the summary describe as the gateway to metareality?
a: Mindfulness that stays with the present moment
Years of formal philosophical study
Mastering creative visualization techniques
A strict daily routine of journaling
questions.why: Lesson 1 says letting past and future fall away so you can focus on now opens the door.

questions.q: What does the summary say about using meditation mainly to reduce stress?
a: It uses only a fraction of meditation's real power
It is the most advanced use of the practice
It works only for people who feel anxious
It makes waking meditation unnecessary
questions.why: Lesson 1 compares it to using a power drill to punch holes in paper.

questions.q: What term does the summary use for turning an idea like money into a physical thing?
a: Reification
Metareality
Conditioning
Projection
questions.why: Lesson 2 calls this process reification, and says we also do it to our own sense of self.

questions.q: What exercise does the summary suggest for getting back in touch with your true self?
a: Having one thought that has never existed before
Writing down your earliest childhood memory
Listing every belief you inherited from family
Spending a week without any media at all
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends one original thought that does not come from any form of media.

questions.q: Where does the author say creativity really comes from?
a: Metareality, which everyone can access
A rare gift given to a chosen few
Luck and sudden flashes of insight
Careful study of society's traditions
questions.why: Lesson 3 says metareality is the true source of creativity, and cites Shakespeare and Van Gogh.
